newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia arrests alleged rebel leader.
newsitem.headline: Colombia arrests alleged rebel leader.

text.p: Colombia's army announced the arrest on Thursday of an accused leftist guerrilla leader suspected of involvement in a failed bomb attack on President Ernesto Samper's official jet.

Army Inspector General Fernando Tapias said Esteban Cancellado Gomez, known by his nom de guerre as "Agustin" and the No. 4 leader of the National Liberation Army ELN, was arrested on Wednesday in the Caribbean port city of Barranquilla.

"He's one of the most important men in the terrorist sector of the guerrillas," Tapias told a news conference at a Bogota military facility where Cancellado, in handcuffs and clad in civilian clothes, was paraded out for local journalists.
Asked by one reporter if he was, in fact, an ELN commander, Cancellado said only, "I am a defender of human rights."

Among other crimes, Tapias said Cancellado was suspected of involvement in a failed bomb attack against Samper's presidential jet in Barranquilla last February and more than 250 dynamite attacks against Colombia's main oil pipeline.
He was also the mastermind behind botched attacks last year against the presidential palace, the defence ministry and National Police headquarters in Bogota, Tapias said.
"He took courses in terrorism and the handling of explosives in Vietnam," the army general said of Cancellado. He did not specify when the training allegedly took place.
The ELN, which specialises in kidnappings and attacks on oil and coal facilities, was founded by radical Roman Catholic priests in 1966.
